resources.string: Shows NEXUS Recent Apps when you press the square button.

NEXUS uses this to run its own Recent Apps screen when you press the square (recent apps) button, and to notice which apps you open so they're listed there. It never takes pictures of your screen: Recent Apps cards are made from each app's icon.

To do that it notes which app (and which of its screens) is in front and where windows are on screen, so it can also step aside for calls, alarms and the screenshot preview. It doesn't read what's in your apps, and it never types or taps anything in them.

If you switch on the NEXUS lock screen (NEXUS Settings → Lock screen), it also shows that screen when your phone's screen turns on. Your phone's own PIN, pattern or fingerprint still unlocks it.

When you swipe apps away in NEXUS Recent Apps, NEXUS closes them fully for you: Android only lets the phone's own recent apps screen do that, so NEXUS briefly opens it behind its own screen and presses Close on those apps' cards (and on any app still open there that NEXUS Recent Apps doesn't show, so the two always match). Apart from the phone's screenshot preview, which it recognises by its words, that is the only screen whose contents NEXUS reads, and only while closing apps. You can switch this off in NEXUS Settings → Recent Apps helper.

If you switch on NEXUS buttons in your apps (NEXUS Settings → Buttons in apps), it shows NEXUS's Back, Home and Recent buttons in place of the phone's own. They only press Back, Home or Recent.

You can turn this off at any time here, or in NEXUS Settings.
